items.title: Why a new report on Anthropic automating AI development is alarming researchers
items.snippet: Anthropic is using AI to build more powerful AI. And it appears to be working remarkably well, with the company's models improving roughly twice as quickly as a year ago, with little indication of slowing down. That's according to a new report published Thursday by the AI safety research organization METR, following an 11-week investigation […]
items.title_ar: تقرير METR: Anthropic تستخدم AI لتطوير AI بسرعة متزايدة
items.summary_ar: وفق تقرير جديد من METR بعد تحقيق استمر 11 أسبوعاً، تستخدم Anthropic الذكاء الاصطناعي لبناء أنظمة أقوى، وتتحسن نماذجها بنحو ضعف السرعة مقارنة بالعام الماضي دون مؤشرات واضحة على التباطؤ.
items.why_ar: يوفر التقرير مؤشراً مهماً على وتيرة تحسن الموديلات الحدودية وما يعنيه ذلك لتخطيط حلول AI.
items.title_en: METR report: Anthropic uses AI to accelerate AI development
items.summary_en: A new METR report, based on an 11-week investigation, finds Anthropic uses AI to build more powerful AI. Its models are improving roughly twice as fast as a year ago, with little sign of slowing.
items.why_en: It offers an important signal on how fast frontier models are improving and what that means for planning AI solutions.

items.title: OpenFrontiers: A Collection of Open Research Problems and a Benchmark for Scientific Rediscovery
items.snippet: Large language models (LLMs) have shown increasing promise in research-level problem solving, yet a comprehensive collection of such problems is still missing, and evaluating them on research-level problems remains challenging. We introduce OpenFrontiers, a cross-disciplinary resource that combines a structured corpus of open research problems with a retrospective benchmark of recently resolved problems in mathematics. The corpus records problem statements, context, progress, and other information for 12,151 problems. items.title_ar: OpenFrontiers: مشكلات بحثية مفتوحة وbenchmark لإعادة الاكتشاف العلمي
items.summary_ar: أطلق الباحثون OpenFrontiers، وهو مورد يجمع corpus منظماً لـ12,151 مشكلة بحثية مفتوحة مع benchmark استعادي يضم 200 مسألة رياضية، منها 110 حُلّت في 2026 و90 ما زالت مفتوحة. كل مسألة في الـbenchmark لها statement بصيغة Lean 4 تم التحقق منه عبر automated probes ومراجعتين مستقلتين.
items.why_ar: يفيدك في تقييم قدرات LLM على مسائل بحثية حقيقية وفي تصميم benchmarks لأبحاثك المنشورة.
items.title_en: OpenFrontiers: open research problems and a scientific rediscovery benchmark
items.summary_en: The researchers released OpenFrontiers, a resource combining a structured corpus of 12,151 open research problems with a retrospective benchmark of 200 mathematics problems, 110 resolved in 2026 and 90 still open. Each benchmark problem has a Lean 4 statement checked by automated probes and two independent reviews.
items.why_en: It gives you a concrete way to evaluate LLM research-level problem solving and a benchmark design you can reference in your own papers.

items.title: Hard Sample-Conditioned Decorrelated Attention for Robust Face Recognition
items.snippet: Multi-head attention in Vision Transformers (ViTs) allows independent attention patterns across heads, but without explicit regularization, heads may learn redundant patterns rather than complementary roles. Correlation-based penalties encourage head disentanglement, yet apply uniform regularization across all training samples. In face recognition (FR), hard samples whose embeddings lie close to competing identities are critical for optimization and generalization. items.title_ar: ViT-HarDis: انتباه متعامد مشروط بصعوبة العينة لتمييز الوجوه
items.summary_ar: تقترح الورقة ViT-HarDis، وهي طريقة تربط إزالة الارتباط بين رؤوس multi-head attention في Vision Transformers بصعوبة العينة. العينات القريبة من مراكز الهويات المنافسة تحصل على تنظيم أقوى لتشجيع تخصص الرؤوس، بهدف تحسين التعرف على الوجوه.
items.why_ar: تقنية تدريب قابلة للتجربة على نماذج Vision Transformer ترتبط بأبحاث التعرف على الوجوه.
items.title_en: Hard Sample-Conditioned Decorrelated Attention for Robust Face Recognition
items.summary_en: The paper proposes ViT-HarDis, which conditions decorrelation of multi-head attention in Vision Transformers on sample difficulty. Samples close to competing identity centers receive stronger head decorrelation to encourage specialization, aiming to improve robust face recognition.
items.why_en: It is a training technique you could test on Vision Transformer models, relevant to face recognition research.
